programme.desc: Julia Bradbury faces the ultimate Wainwright challenge of Scafell Pike. England's highest peak marks the climax of Julia's journey to explore the work, passion and the legacy of Alfred Wainwright, a man who has inspired millions with his illustrated guides to the Lake District. programme.title: The Culture Show
programme.sub-title: The Art of World War II: A Culture Show Special
programme.desc: Despite being locked into a life-or-death struggle, wartime Britain saw an extraordinary explosion of art. programme.title: A Timewatch Guide
programme.desc: Professor Saul David uses the BBC archive to chart the history of the world's most destructive war, by chronicling how the story of the battle has changed. As new information has come to light the history of World War Two evolves.

programme.title: The Sky at Night

programme.title: Andrew Roberts Remembers... AJP Taylor's The War Lords

programme.title: The War Lords
programme.desc: AJP Taylor describes Mussolini's career.

programme.title: The War Lords
programme.desc: The renowned and respected historian AJP Taylor analyses the career of Adolf Hitler - from the birth of his political career to his suicide in 1945 - in this series about the war lords of World War II.

programme.title: Making Their Mark: Six Artists on Drawing
programme.desc: A good drawing consists of the right mark in the right place according to Maggi Hambling, who compares her regular life-drawing sessions to a musician practising scales.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo begins with a tour of the Home Counties and beyond, starting in the city of dreaming spires, Oxford, where in 1921 women were awarded degrees for the first time. programme.title: Wainwright's Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury faces the ultimate Wainwright challenge of Scafell Pike. England's highest peak marks the climax of Julia's journey to explore the work, passion and the legacy of Alfred Wainwright, a man who has inspired millions with his illustrated guides to the Lake District. Before tackling the 3,000ft ascent, Julia seeks advice from fell runner and local sheep farmer, Jos Naylor. Then it's just a case of getting herself and her film crew to the roof of England before darkness falls.
